items.claim: A payload delivered as a JSON request body and parsed with JSON.parse does not pollute the prototype on its own: the parsed object gets `__proto__` as an ordinary own property, so the absence of inherited state on a fresh object is proof the parser was not the vulnerable step.
items.disproof: The rule is wrong when the parsed object is afterwards merged or assigned into another object by a recursive merge or setter-based copy that walks own keys, because at that point the own `__proto__` key is written through the setter and does mutate the prototype; the parser is innocent but the copy is the sink.

sources.quote: The only instance where a piece of JSON text represents a different value from the same JavaScript expression is when dealing with the "__proto__" key
The __proto__ property is just an accessor property on Object.prototype consisting of a getter and setter function.
Tainted data flows from sources to sinks through propagators , such as assignments and function calls.

items.body: Mechanism: A payload delivered as a JSON request body and parsed with JSON.parse does not pollute the prototype on its own: the parsed object gets `__proto__` as an ordinary own property, so the absence of inherited state on a fresh object is proof the parser was not the vulnerable step. How to apply it in the field: treat this as the fp_rule it is — a hunter must be able to state the concrete observation that demonstrates it, with a request and response in hand, before the finding is reportable. Boundary of the rule: The rule is wrong when the parsed object is afterwards merged or assigned into another object by a recursive merge or setter-based copy that walks own keys, because at that point the own `__proto__` key is written through the setter and does mutate the prototype; the parser is innocent but the copy is the sink.

items.claim: Prototype pollution is proved by a property that is visible on an object the test never sent any payload to — a freshly constructed `({})` in the same process returning the injected key — because a successful assignment to the prototype is by definition visible through the whole prototype chain.
items.disproof: The claim is false when the visible property is actually an own property of that object (a framework merged the request body into a shared singleton config, a middleware cached the parsed body on the object, or a test harness reused the same object reference), in which case the value is local, not inherited, and must be distinguished by checking the own-property descriptor rather than the value alone.

sources.quote: The Object.create() static method creates a new object, using an existing object as the prototype of the newly created object.
The __proto__ getter function exposes the value of the internal [[Prototype]] of an object.
Tainted data flows from sources to sinks through propagators , such as assignments and function calls.

items.claim: A validation control that only checks the top-level keys of a request body is bypassed by prototype pollution, because a recursive merge descends into nested objects and the dangerous key can sit several levels down where the allowlist never looked.
items.disproof: The rule is false when the check is applied recursively at every depth and the merge refuses to recurse into any key that is not a plain string-keyed object, or when the merge never treats `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` as writable slots; then the nested payload cannot reach the prototype and the shallow-check bypass does not exist.

sources.quote: The rule specifies the sanitizer sanitize_input(...) , so any expression that matches that pattern is considered sanitized.
The __proto__ setter allows the [[Prototype]] of an object to be mutated.

items.claim: An application that explicitly defines `__proto__` as an own property on one object via Object.defineProperty has not polluted anything: the accessor is shadowed for that object only, and the prototype chain of every other object is unchanged.
items.disproof: The claim is false when the same call is made on `Object.prototype` itself rather than on an instance, or when the application assigns through the accessor on a shared prototype object; those two cases mutate the chain globally and are genuine pollution despite the identical call syntax.

sources.quote: Furthermore, __proto__ can be redefined as an own property on any object instance through Object.defineProperty() without triggering the setter.
The rule specifies the sanitizer sanitize_input(...) , so any expression that matches that pattern is considered sanitized.
The Object.create() static method creates a new object, using an existing object as the prototype of the newly created object.

items.claim: The evidence that identifies a prototype-pollution vulnerability is the specific merge, deep-assign or setter use on the tainted value, not the input format, because the same JSON body is inert without that sink and a different body format is equally exploitable against it.
items.disproof: The claim is false when the vulnerable component itself performs the merge internally on raw bytes — a framework's own body-parsing middleware, an ORM deserialising into a typed model — because there the input format is the entire attack surface and no distinct sink code exists to point at.
